topic: coupling and coherence measurement, revised (retraction of the 8 dB claim)

measurement.source: white noise, direct playback, -6 dBFS nominal
measurement.note: each run 2.42 s so the 0.336 s tail sits inside the 2.4 s source

reliable_peak.caveat: based on a single spectral bin; statistically weak

retraction.withdrawn: peak coupling +1.73 dB at 453 Hz / +2.34 dB at 381 Hz and the derived 'about 8 dB of cancellation is required' conclusion
retraction.reason: those estimates came from bins with coherence near 0.3; the ratio |Gxy|/Gxx is unreliable where the microphone signal is mostly uncorrelated noise
retraction.replacement: no trustworthy quantitative cancellation target yet; the measurement must reach coherence >= 0.8 across the band first

what_stands: broadband cross-correlation between reference and microphone is about 0.10 in both earlier captures
coherence is highest at 4-8 kHz (mean 0.63 after raising the source to -6 dBFS), so the usable linear path is high-frequency
raising the source from -18 to -6 dBFS improved coherence at 4-8 kHz from about 0.45 to 0.63
next: swept-sine or averaged long capture to reach coherence >= 0.8 before any model fit
model_status: no valid model. model_room_side_100cm_v1.json and model_room_side_100cm_lowband_v1.json are artifacts of an inadequate measurement and must not be used on the board
